name: satteri-scoped-references
instr:
Please add opt-in lexical scopes for Markdown reference definitions in `/app`, so a section or quoted passage can use its own link targets without changing the rest of the document. Expose `satteri_pulldown_cmark::Options::ENABLE_SCOPED_REFERENCES` as a `pub const ENABLE_SCOPED_REFERENCES: Options`; it is off by default. Don't add new crates.

The document is the outer scope. Each ATX or setext heading opens a section, including the heading itself, which ends at the next heading of equal or lower level in the same container. Blockquotes, individual list items, footnote definitions and container directives each introduce a nested scope; sections inside one of these cannot extend beyond it or close sections outside it. Other nodes, including JSX elements, do not introduce scopes. Definitions belong to the innermost scope containing their opening bracket. Resolve a reference in its innermost scope, then its ancestors, using the first matching definition in each scope regardless of whether it appears before or after the reference. Use the parser's existing label matching and decoding rules.

Apply this to link and image references through both `Parser` and the arena parsing entry points. In scoped mode, arena references that resolve become ordinary `Link` or `Image` nodes carrying the chosen URL and title, while definitions remain `Definition` nodes. Keep their complete reference source spans and the usual inline children or image alt text. For example, with `[r]: /root` before `
